title: Size a pgbouncer+postgres stack to survive a 50/100/200 client connection ladder
goal: The sealed grader drives pgbench in select-only mode with per-transaction reconnects (-C) through pgbouncer at 50, then 100, then 200 concurrent clients; the starter pgbouncer.ini is undersized on every axis and collapses at the first rung. You must do real capacity planning: reason about pool mode versus reconnect churn, client connection limits versus postgres max_connections, and pool sizing versus available server slots, then encode that plan in assets/gc-380/tuned/pgbouncer.ini and tuned/postgresql.conf. All three stages must complete with nonzero throughput and no error abort, and the 200-client stage must retain at least half the 50-client throughput, so a config that merely queues everything into a trickle also fails. Validate each rung yourself before invoking the sealed ladder, and iterate on the failures it exposes.
process_expectations: A capacity plan artifact exists before tuning: expected connection math (clients vs max_client_conn vs pool size vs max_connections) written down per ladder rung
Each rung is tested in isolation with self-run pgbench commands and the raw tps/error output is captured before the full sealed ladder is attempted
Failure identities are recorded (e.g. 'rung 2: max_client_conn exhausted', 'rung 3: server slots saturated in session mode'), with the config change that addressed each
Throughput-retention analysis (tps@200 vs tps@50) is computed by the agent from its own runs, not first discovered via the sealed grader
The sealed grader's stages_ok trajectory across attempts is logged honestly, including collapses after config changes
